ubi non tantùm utriusq; Lingua, sed

traditur, & in quo nos studiorum tyroci-
nium posuimus; post perceptam Linguam
Latinam atq; Græcam, & Rhetorico
quoq; ac Logico stadio decurso, ordine ad
Rerum Naturalium disciplinam pervenissemus: una cum eâ
magna quoq; Aristotelis admiratio nobis instillata fuit, tanquam

cognoscenda putavimus, nedum ut scripta eorum nobis tractan-
da aut vel inspicienda existimaremus. Hoc in Ar-
istotelem studium, atq; reliquorum, qui ab eo dissentirent, aver-
satio, duravit nobis etiam, postquam in tuum, Alma Mater,
sinum nos recepimus, atq; ibi Hippocrati ac Galeno nos in Me-
dicinæ disciplinam tradidimus. Quippe & inter initia, dum

page.notes: Woodcut initial Q with a figure in an oval frame; the initial letter is read as Q. Transcription of the opening word "VUm" reads as "Cum" with the large initial. The word "stant" at the foot right is the final word of the page, not a catchword in the strict sense; the last line is incomplete and continues on the next page. Some faint speckles and marks in the margins are not printed text.
